column1: # The parity matrix of Desk Writer: every row of the survey of Pages '09,
# the 33 cases of integration of the three surveys (IOP), what the
# GNOME HIG and desktop ask of the apps (GNM), and the commands that the
# inventory of Pages 4.3 on the reference virtual machine added to the
# survey (VMI), each with the phase of the old plan that completes it
# (- when out of scope), and the features of Pages 15 as Pages 15.4 does
# them on the owner's Mac, seen on 2026-11-18 (PXV, D-020), each with the
# phase of docs/roadmap.md that builds it, such as W1.
# Tab-separated; the surveys, the roadmap, the review of 2026-11-07 and
# the inventory of 2026-11-14 are the sources.
# The gnome column says how Desk adapts a row to GNOME where the
# 2026-11-16 (window M+, D-008, and automatic saving) changed its form; the row passes
# when Desk does it that way.

column4: expected
column7: gnome

column4: Opens when the app starts. Templates grouped by category for both kinds of document. "Choose" creates a new document from the template.
column7: Template gallery inside the empty window, without a window of its own; Ctrl+N creates from the default template and Ctrl+Shift+N opens a window on the gallery (path E)

column4: The text flows in the body from page to page. Takes a table of contents and floating or inline objects. Thumbnails hidden and only the horizontal ruler shown by default.
Has no body text. The text is in text boxes, which can be linked, and every object floats. Thumbnails and the horizontal and vertical rulers shown by default.
column6: Partial: the kind of document must be marked

column4: One click selects all the placeholder text, and typing replaces it. An image, sound or movie dragged onto the media placeholder takes its size and position.
column6: Partial: media placeholders need an extension

column4: Objects repeated in the background of the pages, such as watermarks and logos. They cannot be selected during normal editing.
The Pages or Sections button inserts a page of the template right after the insertion point.
View > Zoom menu and a zoom menu in the bottom left corner. The default zoom is set in Preferences, under Rulers.
column7: M+: a zoom control overlaid on a corner of the document, besides the View menu

column4: One Page, Two Pages, Fit Width and Fit Page.
Shows the outlines of headers, footers, columns, text boxes and body, and shows rulers and guides.

Space, non-breaking space, tab, line breaks, paragraph, page, column, layout and section breaks, and object anchor. Configurable color. Selecting an invisible and deleting it removes the formatting it stands for.

Buttons for Pages or Sections, Comment, Outline, Share, Inspector, Media, Colors, Fonts, objects, View and Full Screen. Items can be added, removed and reordered, with small icons or text only as options.
column7: Header bar of M+ (D-008): at the start, the Sidebar button, the Insert menu and the six object buttons Table, Chart, Text, Shape, Media and Comment; the window title in the middle, with the folder as subtitle; at the end, Open documents, Find, Inspector and the main menu. No customization (path A). Below 720 px the object buttons go into the Insert menu. There is no format bar: Fonts and Colors are in the Format pane of the Inspector

column4: The controls change with the selection. For text: Styles Drawer, paragraph and character style, font, typeface, size, color, alignment, spacing, columns and list.
column7: M+: there is no format bar. What it held is in the Format pane of the Inspector, whose first tab is that of the selection (text, object, table cell, chart), as in iWork 15

column4: Document, Layout, Wrap, Text, Graphic, Metrics, Table, Chart, Link and QuickTime. Several Inspector windows can be open at once.
column7: One Inspector, in the right sidebar, without New Inspector (path C). In M+ the choice at the top of the pane is Format and Document; under Format, the tabs of what is selected (text: Style, Layout and More; image: Style, Image and Arrange; shape: Style, Text and Arrange; table: Table, Cell, Text and Arrange; chart: Chart, Axis, Series and Arrange); under Document, the tabs Document, Section and Info

column4: Gives access to the libraries of photos, music and movies, with search and extra folders. Items are dragged to the page or to an image well of the Inspector.
column7: M+: popover of the Media button of the header bar, with Pictures, Music and Videos, search, the folders the person adds and Choose File; a click inserts and dragging takes the item to the page

column4: Family, typeface, size and collections. Underline and strikethrough effects (single or double), text color, paragraph background color, and shadow with opacity, blur, offset and angle.
column7: Popover on the font button of the Format pane, also by Ctrl+T, in place of the window (path D); collections All, Favorites (by the star), Fixed Width and Recently Used

column4: Color wheel, color models, brightness, opacity, saved palette and an eyedropper on the screen.
column7: Palette on the color buttons of the Format pane and the full chooser by Ctrl+Shift+C, in place of the window that stays open (path D)

column4: The horizontal ruler (and the optional vertical one) controls indents, tabs, margins and columns. Guides appear while objects move.
Lists with a preview the paragraph, character and list styles. Applies and creates styles, and hides the list and character styles.
column7: M+: the Styles page of the navigation sidebar, by its content switcher, by the View menu and by Ctrl+Shift+T, in place of the drawer

column4: Previous and next page arrows and a menu to navigate by section, comment, link or style. "Go to Page" field, thumbnails and the Page Up, Page Down, Home and End keys.
column7: M+: the page thumbnails are in the navigation sidebar; Go to Page and Navigate By are in the View menu

column4: Search in Spotlight, statistics, dictionary and thesaurus, and search in Google or Wikipedia, also from the context menu.
List of shortcuts in Help. Control-click opens the context menu, much used in tables and charts.
column7: Context menu by the right button, the Menu key and Shift+F10; the list of shortcuts is the shortcuts dialog of GNOME (Ctrl+?)

column4: Lists what was not imported or saved correctly. Replaces a missing font and copies the warnings.
column7: Banner with View Warnings when something may not look as it was made, which Preferences can turn off; the list opens in a dialog, with Copy and Clear All, also from Document Warnings in the main menu (path I)

column4: On-screen help, video tutorials and tips when the pointer rests.
column7: Help in the GNOME format, opened by F1, which GNOME reserves for it

column4: The user picks a category and a template. Moving the pointer over the icon goes through the pages of the template, and a slider changes the size of the icons. There is a "Blank" template for each kind of document.
Show the Template Chooser or always open a chosen template.
From the Chooser, by File > Open, from the recent ones, by double click or by dragging onto the icon of the app.
Opens documents of iWork '05, '06 and '08. New features require saving in the '09 format.
column6: Out of scope: Desk reads only the format of iWork '09

column4: The document opens anyway. Missing fonts are replaced and recorded in the Warnings window.
.txt, .rtf/.rtfd, AppleWorks 6 (.cwk) and Word (.doc; the guide cites Office 2007). From Word come styles, tables, objects, charts, notes, bookmarks, links, lists, sections and tracked changes.

Word and page count at the bottom. The format bar and the menus appear at the top, and the thumbnails on the left, when the pointer gets there. There are View and Background controls. Esc leaves, and the document always reopens in the normal mode.
column7: F11 enters and leaves full screen

column4: Require password to open in the Document Inspector, with the Password Assistant, a padlock beside the title and options to change and remove the password.

column3: Save and Save a Copy As
column4: Option to save a copy in the Word format. "Include preview in document" makes the thumbnail of the file.
Copy audio and movies into the document or only link them. Copy or not the images of the template into the document.
column6: Partial: images of the template not copied

column4: Saves by itself while editing, and Cmd-S keeps a version. "Browse All Versions" shows a timeline. An old version can be restored whole, compared side by side, or have objects and settings copied from it.
column7: Automatic saving and versions, as in iWork 15 (D-001): the document saves itself, and the versions are browsed and restored from the main menu

column4: Unlimited undo since opening, and File > Revert to Saved.
The template then shows in My Templates in the Chooser.
Creates an untitled copy open beside the original (in Snow Leopard, Save As).
Preference that keeps "Backup of <name>" with the earlier version. Only the last version is kept.
A document saved in outline mode reopens in that mode.
Prevents accidental editing until the user unlocks it.
With Option, closes all. Asks to save if there are changes.
column7: Asks "Save changes?" with Cancel | Discard | Save, as GNOME does (decision of 13 November)

column4: Author, title, comments and keywords, indexed by the search of the system.
Words, pages, lines, paragraphs, sections, graphics and characters, of the document or of the selection. Words and pages show at the foot of the window, which can be turned off in Preferences.
column7: M+: the count is overlaid at the foot of the document and shows that of the selection when text is selected

column4: Size, location and the dates of creation and change.
Reading and writing the original format is a requirement of the project, but the guide does not describe it. The specification comes from outside sources and from tests on the virtual machine.

One click selects the whole area, and the text typed takes its style. In a text box, the first click selects the box and the second the text. In a table, the cell needs a double click. Deleting with the box or the table selected removes the placeholder.
column6: Partial: placeholders in boxes and tables

column4: In word processing, the content of the page or the whole section is deleted (from the thumbnails or by Edit > Delete Page, with a confirmation). In page layout, the pages are selected in the thumbnails.
column7: Deleting a page deletes the whole section of the page, with a confirmation, as Pages 4.3 does (checked on the Lion virtual machine on 13 November)

column4: Drag, double click (word), triple click (paragraph), Shift-click (block), Shift-Option-arrow (to the start or the end of the paragraph), Shift-arrow, and Cmd for discontinuous selections.
Paste keeps the style of the source. "Paste and Match Style" takes the style of the destination.
Keyboard Viewer and the Characters window of the system, also for Chinese, Japanese and Korean.
column7: Special Characters (Ctrl+.) opens the emoji and symbol chooser of GTK; other characters come from the Characters app of GNOME or from Ctrl+Shift+U

column4: Preference that turns straight quotes into curly opening and closing quotes.

Fix capitals, superscript ordinals (1st, 2nd), detect email addresses and URLs as links (a preference of the computer, not of the document), detect lists, take the single suggestion of the spelling checker, and a table of replacements, such as (c) for ©, each on or off.
Option-Space.

On by default. Can be turned off in the document or the paragraph. Per word, "Never Hyphenate" applies to every occurrence. Pages keeps the word in the preferences of the user, and Desk keeps it in the document.
column6: Extension: document and exceptions per word

column4: Dashed red underline while typing. Check from the cursor to the end or only in the selection, with Cmd-; to go on. Window with suggestions and the actions Correct, Ignore, Learn and Forget. The language is set per run of text.
column7: Spelling and Grammar as a page of the right sidebar, in place of the window (path I)

column4: Works while typing or on demand. Points out capitals, punctuation, repeated words, wordy phrases, formatting, parts of speech, jargon, misspellings and gendered expressions.
column7: The proofreader is on the same page of the sidebar, without a window of its own (path I)

column4: Simple and Advanced modes. Replace All, Replace, Replace & Find, Next and Previous, Use Selection for Find and Jump to Selection.
column7: Search bar in the window by Ctrl+F, or by Ctrl+H already with Replace, on a second row; the options of the Advanced mode in a popover, which inserts a tab and a line break, shown as ⇥ and ↵ (path F)

column4: Lists the matches as the user types, with page and context, in the body, headers, tables, boxes, shapes, notes and comments. Options Match Case and Whole Words, the last 10 searches, and editing from the result. Does not search invisibles.
column7: M+: the Search Results page of the navigation sidebar, by Ctrl+Alt+F (path F)

column4: Only in word processing. Return creates a topic and Tab a subtopic, up to 9 levels, with Promote and Demote. Options to truncate to the first line, show objects as thumbnails and choose the levels shown. Dragging the control moves the topic with its subtopics. The controls are not printed.

Tracks: text in the body, headers, footers, notes, shapes, boxes and cells; inline tables, charts and shapes; floating objects added, moved or resized; formulas and cell formats; styles and formatting; links, merge fields, placeholders, bookmarks and the table of contents.
column6: Partial: objects and cells need an extension

column4: Sits under the format bar, with the comments and changes pane, navigation arrows, Pause, the markup menu, Accept, Reject and the actions menu.

column3: Turn on, pause and turn off
column4: Pause keeps the earlier changes and stops recording new ones. Turning off requires accepting or rejecting what is pending.

Bubbles with author, date and kind, and change bars when the pane is hidden. Bubbles of the selection only and formatting bubbles are optional. Modes Show Markup, Show Markup Without Deletions and Final. Author color and name and markup styles can be set. Thumbnails highlight the changes.

Tracks content, formulas, images, format, background and opacity. Does not track rows and columns, borders, merging, splitting or autofill. A mark in the corner of the cell in the color of the author, gray when there are several authors.
Per bubble, from the bar, from the context menu, by the selection (text or cells) or all at once.
Makes a copy with everything accepted and no comments, keeping the tracking in the original.

Anchored at the cursor, on a selection, on an object or on a cell. The bubble grows with the text and takes styles. Inserting a comment shows all of them. They print when shown, with the page fitted to make room.
From the format bar, the Format menu and the Fonts window. Single or double underline.
Single or double, with a color of its own apart from the color of the text.
Opacity, blur, offset and angle, from the Fonts window or the Graphic Inspector.
Format > Font > Outline. The guide warns that it may look different in other programs.
Bigger and Smaller in steps of 1 pt, or an exact value in the Fonts window.
Subscript and superscript (with a smaller font), Raise and Lower, and an exact shift in points.
All Caps, Small Caps, Title (first letter of each word) and None.
Typography window with the features of the font (as Zapfino and Hoefler Text).
Default, None or All, per selection. "Use ligatures" in the document and "Remove ligatures" in the paragraph or style.
Tracking in percent, from the Text Inspector or Format > Font.
From the bar, the Inspector or the Fonts window. The last tool used wins.
Left, center, right and justified. In cells there is "Auto Align": text on the left and numbers on the right.
Top, middle or bottom in text boxes, shapes and cells.
Single, Double, Multiple, At Least, Exactly (between baselines) and Between (adds space without making the line taller).

column3: Space before and after a paragraph
column4: Between two paragraphs the larger of the two values applies, not their sum. The space before the first paragraph of a box, shape or cell is ignored.
column6: Extension: rule of the larger value

column4: Left, center, right and decimal, with a configurable decimal character and a dashed or dotted leader. From the ruler (a click creates, a double click changes the kind, dragging out deletes) or the Inspector. Default distance of half an inch.
Units, percent of the page, origin at the center and vertical ruler. They apply to every document.
column7: The default unit follows the locale (centimetres in pt-BR), and an open document keeps its own measures

column4: First line, left and right, from the ruler or the Inspector, hanging indent included. Option moves the margin without moving the indent.
The same space on the four sides between the text and the edge of boxes, shapes and cells.
The background of the paragraph reaches between the margins of the layout and follows the text.
Line style, color and thickness. Rule above, below or both, or a border around, with an adjustable distance from the text.
Sets the spelling and hyphenation dictionary per paragraph, run or style.
•, "-", "*", "+", "1.", "1)", "a." or "I." followed by a space and Return start the list, whose bullet keeps the character typed. Can be turned off in Preferences.

Tab and Shift-Tab change the level with the children. With Option, only the item changes. Dragging the bullet puts the item on another level. Return twice ends the list, and Shift-Return makes a paragraph without a bullet.
column7: Alt+Shift+Right and Alt+Shift+Left change only the item, in place of Option+Tab, because Alt+Tab switches windows in GNOME (decision of 14 November)

column4: Text (with a color), an image of the app or an image of one's own. Size in percent or "Scale with text". Indent of the bullet and of the text, and vertical alignment of the bullet.
Arabic, Roman or letters, with adjustable indents. Options Continue from Previous and Start At.
1, 1.1, 1.1.1 or I, A, 1, a), (1)... with a style of its own on each of the 9 levels.
Paragraph (font, spacing, shadow, background, indents, tabs, breaks and next style), character and list. A list style sets only bullets and indents, and the look of the text comes from the paragraph.
From the Drawer or the bar. A new paragraph style replaces the list style. Character styles survive a change of paragraph style. Selecting a box, table, cell or shape applies it to all of its text.
column7: Paragraph and character styles in the Style tab of the Format pane and on the Styles page of the sidebar

column3: Creating a style from the selection
column4: For a paragraph, it starts from "Free Form". For a character style, the attributes that go into the style are chosen, for example only those that differ from the paragraph. There is an option not to apply it when it is created.
Each style can have a shortcut. With Option, the shortcut applies the style and clears the overrides.
column7: Shortcuts Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+8 in place of F1 to F8, and Ctrl+Shift+1 to 8 in place of Option+F1 to F8, because GNOME reserves F1, F9, F10 and Alt with the function keys (decision of 14 November)

column4: Deleting a style in use asks for a replacement.
column7: Only the default style cannot be deleted; a style listed in the table of contents can, and the table of contents updates, as on the Lion virtual machine (where the Blank template also protects Heading 1 to 3)

column4: A red arrow in the Drawer shows an override. "Redefine Style from Selection" and "Revert to Defined Style" (or a double click on the name). Redefining the paragraph does not change the character styles applied.
column7: Revert to the style and the double click remove the overrides and the character styles of the whole paragraph, as on the Lion virtual machine

column4: Paragraph style applied by itself after Return.
column7: Next paragraph style in the menu of each style of the Styles page

column4: For paragraphs and characters, also between documents, without changing the content.
Select All Uses in the body. Advanced Find also replaces styles in boxes and shapes.

Imports the styles chosen from another document. "Replace duplicates" overwrites; without it, the imported one becomes "Body 2". Text in locked objects changes style but keeps its look. Word styles come with the document.
Settings of the whole document: page, margins, headers and footers on, kind of note, space between notes, hyphenation, ligatures and password.
From Page Setup. The Blank templates exist in portrait and landscape.
1 inch on the four sides by default, shown in gray in the layout view.
In word processing, makes a page in the same section. In page layout, adds a page, which is a new section.
Starts on a new page, keep with next, keep lines together, and avoid widows and orphans.
Shift-Return.
Up to 10 columns, of equal or individual width, with a gutter of its own between each pair. A menu of up to 4 columns in the bar, and adjustment by the ruler.
Continues the text in the next column. In a layout of one column, goes to the top of the next page.
Ends a layout and starts another with columns and margins of its own, without changing headers or numbering. Option "Layout starts on new page".
Left, right, before and after the layout, always inside the margins of the page.
Inside and outside margins, and a side-by-side view, also in the thumbnails.
Text, images and fields, repeated on every page of the section. They can differ on the first page and between left and right pages. Option "Use previous headers and footers".

One kind per document: footnotes, end of document or end of section, with conversion among them. Numbering in Arabic, Roman or symbols (*, †, ‡), continuous or restarted per page or section. Notes take inline objects.
column6: Partial: endnotes at the end of sections

column4: A mark chosen by the user, without automatic numbering. Switches between a custom mark and an automatic one.
Notes and marks use styles. The space between notes can be set. A double click goes from the mark to the note and back.
Made by section breaks. In page layout, each page is a section. Master objects, headers, footers and numbering apply only to their own section.
A yellow frame surrounds the section. Several can be selected, cut, copied, pasted, duplicated, dragged (Option copies) and deleted with a confirmation.
column7: Select All (Ctrl+A) in the thumbnails; Ctrl+drag copies sections, the dragging convention of GTK, in place of Option

column4: Option "Start at" in the Section pane.
Different header, footer and master objects on the first page and on left and right pages. The section can start on a left, right or any page.
Format > Advanced > Capture Pages saves pages of a section in the Pages or Sections menu, by name.
Move Object to Section Master and "Make Master Objects Selectable". When selectable they have blue handles.

Uses the paragraph styles marked in the Table of Contents pane, with an optional page number per style and the numbers as links. Each table of contents lists only the content up to the next one. Updates on a click on an entry, on "Update Now" or when the document closes.
column6: Partial: scope up to the next table of contents

column4: Entries of the same level are selected together. Table of contents styles of their own in the Drawer, and a leader line up to the number.

Search for citations, hide author or year, page range, prefix and suffix, "Bibliography only". The bibliography is made at the end and updates by itself, one per document. Linux has no EndNote, and the natural equivalent is Zotero.
To a web page, an email with recipient and subject, a bookmark of the document or another document (optionally at a bookmark of it). Option "Make all links inactive" to edit the text.
Made from the selection. A list sortable by name or page, with go to, rename and delete.

Page number and page count with a format, date and time with a format and "Update on open", and file name with optional path and extension. "Auto Page Numbers" inserts the number with position, alignment and the option to leave it out on the first page.

A floating object is fixed to the page and the text goes around it. An inline object follows the text, with its top and left handles inactive. Inside shapes, boxes and cells only inline objects go. The conversion is made from the bar or the Wrap Inspector.
The formats of QuickTime (TIFF, GIF, JPEG, PDF, PSD, EPS, PICT). Drag from the file manager or the Media Browser, or Insert > Choose. Cmd while dragging inserts inline.
Dragging an image replaces it, already sized, placed and framed. Edit Mask adjusts the framing. An option sets or unsets the placeholder.
Rectangular by default, or a predefined or drawn shape. The image can be resized and moved inside the mask, and the mask rotated (Cmd). Edit Mask and Unmask.
Keeps only the part used of cropped or reduced images, of one image or the whole document. Cannot be undone and does not apply to image fills.

Clicking and dragging over a color makes the contiguous area of similar colors transparent, and the more one drags, the larger the area. With Option, removes every occurrence of the color. Can be reverted at any time.
Non-destructive: brightness, contrast, saturation, temperature, tint, sharpness, exposure, a histogram with levels, automatic Enhance and Reset.
Circle, rectangles, star, callouts, arrows, polygon and lines. Floating from the bar and inline from the Insert menu. Option-click draws at the size, and Shift keeps the proportions.
Each click adds a point, and Delete undoes the last segment. Clicking the first point closes the shape. Esc or a double click leaves it open, and it can be continued later.

Make Editable shows red points. Option adds a point, Shift selects several. Curves have handles: Option moves both together and Cmd only one. A double click switches between corner and curve. Smooth Path and Sharpen Path apply to the whole shape.
Corners of the rounded rectangle, proportion between head and tail of arrows, corners and tail of callouts, points and angle of the star, and sides of the polygon, by a slider.
column6: Partial: number of points and sides

column4: Every shape takes text, except lines, with a mark when the text does not fit. A rotated shape can keep its text horizontal. In a resized group, the text does not change size.
column6: Partial: horizontal text in a rotated shape

column4: Made by the Text Box button, or drawn with Option-click. Cmd-Return leaves editing and selects the box. Its edges show only in the layout view. It can be locked.
Only in word processing, by Insert > Text Box. Does not grow with its text.

The blue square links the box to another or makes a new one, and Esc cancels. Selected boxes can also be linked, in the order of selection, and the incoming or outgoing link broken. The text follows the order of the links, not the position. Copying the whole chain keeps the links. Cmd-A selects the text of the chain.
Number of columns, equal or individual width, and gutter.

Floating: around, only on the side with more room, left, right, or above and below. Inline: six positions, with or without text beside. Tight or loose wrap by the alpha channel, extra space and transparency threshold. Tables take no text beside them.
column6: Partial: outline by the alpha channel

column4: MOV, MP3, MPEG-4, AIFF and AAC, floating or inline. Sound shows as a speaker icon and plays on a double click.
From the QuickTime Inspector: start and stop, poster frame, repeat (none, loop, back and forth), volume and preview controls.
Removes the parts outside the start and stop. Cannot be undone.

Click (on an object without a fill, on its edge). Shift adds to the selection, as long as all are floating or all inline. Cmd-A outside the text selects all floating objects. Cmd-drag reaches objects behind the text.
Copy and paste, Option-drag, or Duplicate (a copy slightly offset). Inline objects cannot be duplicated.
column7: Alt+drag copies, like Option+drag: GNOME moves windows with Super+drag, so there is no conflict; Alt+arrows still duplicate

column4: Shift restricts the move to horizontal, vertical or 45°. Arrows move 1 pt, and 10 pt with Shift. A preference shows size and position during the move.
Bring Forward and Send Backward, one level at a time or to the end of the stack.
In word processing, an object sent to the background can no longer be selected, until the user turns on "Background objects selectable".
Left, center, right, top, middle and bottom, by the box that surrounds every selected object: Left goes to its leftmost edge, Center to its center. Distribute horizontally or vertically.
Appear at the center and, if turned on in Preferences, at the edges while dragging, blue by default, with a configurable color. Cmd hides them, and they are not printed.
Made by dragging from the ruler and removed by dragging out. Each guide belongs to the page it was made on. They show on the page while editing.
x and y of the top left corner of the bounding box, even with the object rotated. Lines have start and end coordinates.
Floating objects only. The text stays editable inside the group, and successive clicks reach objects of nested groups.
Joins two objects and follows them when they move. Can be curved by its middle point and keep a gap at each end.
Floating only. A locked object can be selected and copied, and the copy is locked too.
Option resizes from the center and Shift keeps the proportions. "Constrain proportions" option, exact measures (also for several objects) and Original Size.
Flip horizontally or vertically. Rotate with Cmd and a handle (Shift in steps of 45°) or by the angle wheel. Inline tables do not rotate.
Solid, dotted, dashed and other lines, with thickness, color and endpoints such as arrows and circles.
A library of graphic frames with an adjustable thickness, for images, movies, boxes, shapes and placeholders.
Angle, offset, blur, opacity and color. Shows over the objects behind.
A vertical reflection downward, with an adjustable intensity.
The opacity of the object apart from that of the fill and the stroke. That of the color works as a maximum, and that of the object is relative to it.
A color with opacity in shapes, tables, cells and chart elements.
Linear of two colors, with angle and reversal. The advanced one has several colors, blend points and a radial mode with an adjustable center.
Scale to Fit, Scale to Fill, Stretch, Original Size and Tile, and a tinted image (a color with opacity). Applies to shapes, boxes, tables, cells, background and chart series.
Inserted and edited with a double click and treated as an image, which can be moved, rotated, grouped or masked. Linux has no MathType, and the natural way is an editor of its own that saves MathML.
By the button or the Insert menu. With Option-click, the table is drawn, and rows and columns follow the size. Dragging selected cells out makes a new table with the values.
Format bar, Table Inspector (structure, borders, background, headers, options), Format pane (formats and rules), context menu, Formula Editor and Function Browser.

Handles (Shift keeps the proportions, Option resizes from the center). Exact measures, rotation and distance from the margins in the Metrics Inspector, the only way when the table crosses pages. Option-dragging the border copies the table.
Background of the table or of the cells, borders and text. Copy and Paste Table Style.
Converting text, each Return becomes a row and each tab a column. Also converts a table to text.
The table keeps its look, data and attributes. Hidden rows and columns do not show in the other app, and comments are not copied.

Table (Cmd-Return comes back from the cell), cell, range (Shift or dragging), separate cells (Cmd), rows and columns. Borders: successive clicks switch between the long border and the segment, and dragging a border moves it.

column3: Navigation and "Return moves to next cell"
column4: Tab, Shift-Tab, the arrows and Return follow the table of rules on page 183. Tab in the last cell makes a row or a column, as the option of the table says.
As it grows, the table pushes the neighbouring objects, which can be turned off in Preferences.
Above, below, before or after, as many as are selected. New rows go above the footer. If every cell above has the same formula, it is repeated in the new row.
From the Format menu, the Inspector or the bar.

Up to 5 header rows, 5 header columns and 5 footer rows. The corner belongs to the row header. Headers can repeat on each page, column or box, and editing one changes all. The names of the headers serve as references in formulas.
Distribute evenly (even not adjacent), exact height and width, and "Resize to fit content".
Bands in a chosen color, and the other rows use the background of the cell.

Ascending or descending by one column, in the whole table or only the selected cells. Headers stay out, and hidden rows go in. Order by kind: numbers before text, empty cells at the end, booleans between text and empty cells.
Typing replaces the content, and a double click edits a part. Esc undoes what was typed since the selection. "Clear All" removes content, background and style.
Suggests completions with values of the same column (can be turned off). Option-Return breaks the line and Option-Tab inserts a tab.
Takes digits and + − ( ) / currency % . E and e. Long decimals are rounded and large integers go to scientific notation.
The handle copies value, format, formula and background, but not comments. Fill right, left, up or down. Continues sequences of days, months and progressions from two or more cells.
A "+" mark in the corner. Without text wrap and without automatic fitting, the content spills into empty neighbouring cells.

Rules for numbers, text and dates, with a fixed value or a reference to a cell, also of another table. Applies text color, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough and background. With several rules, the first from the top wins for each attribute. Selects the cells with the same rule, clears and copies rules.
Color, gradient or image.
Only rectangles of cells of the same kind (body, header or footer). The content is joined with tabs horizontally or paragraphs vertically, and the background comes from the top or left cell.
Into two equal rows or two equal columns. The text stays in the first part.
Style, thickness and color per segment, or a hidden border.
Dragging moves and replaces the destination, and Option-dragging copies. Works in the same table, between tables or onto the page.
Show, hide and print, as the other comments.

Automatic, Number, Currency (with an accounting style), Percentage (3 becomes 300%), Date and Time, Duration, Fraction, Numeral System (bases 2 to 36, with two's complement), Scientific and Text. The format changes only the display, and formulas use the real value.

Draggable elements: integers, currency, decimals or fractions, spaces (normal, wide, narrow, flexible) and scale (percent, hundreds, thousands, millions, billions, trillions, scientific). They take fixed text and conditions by value.
Built from elements and applied when the value typed has a hyphen or a slash.
Edit, rename, reorder and delete. Editing or renaming a format changes it in every cell that has it; deleting it asks first and gives those cells the Automatic format (Pages 15.4, 21 November).
Formula Editor, Function Browser and references by header name. The details are in the iWork formulas guide, which has to be obtained.
Column, stacked column, bar, stacked bar, line, area, stacked area and pie, all in 2D and 3D. Besides them, scatter, mixed and 2-axis.
Rows vs. Columns changes what a series is. A pie uses only the first value of each series, and a scatter chart uses x,y pairs.

column3: Creating a chart and the Data Editor
column4: Inline or floating (floating only in page layout). Option-click draws the chart. It starts with sample data in a separate table that does not show on the page. There the labels and values are edited, reordered by dragging, rows and columns added and deleted, and data from spreadsheets pasted.

Keeps axes, grid, tick marks, number format, borders, rotation, shadows and 3D lighting. Back to the default: value labels, text style, stroke, shadow, fill and symbols of the series. In a scatter chart, an odd series left over is ignored.

column3: Editing the data of a chart
column4: From the Inspector or by Format > Chart, with an immediate update.
Pasted from Numbers, it stays linked to its source tables. The Refresh button reloads the data after Numbers saves. There is an Unlink option and a "Source" link that opens the Numbers document.
Show or hide, edit in place and drag. The labels of the legend can be edited in the legend or the Data Editor.
Clicking the chart formats every title and label at once. One series, one axis or the legend can also be formatted alone.
2D charts rotate (Cmd and a handle, Shift-Cmd in steps of 45°, or by the Metrics Inspector). 3D ones neither rotate nor flip.

Grid and tick marks, maximum and minimum (or Auto), steps, labels, minimum value and number format of the axis. Categories labelled every N, with an option to show the last. Axis titles and a linear, logarithmic or percent scale, by the type.
Collections of colors and textures (as marble and wood), applied to every series or dragged onto one. Opacity, stroke and shadow per series.
Position, format, negatives and decimal places.

In every 2D chart but the pie: positive and negative, positive only or negative only. By a fixed value, percent, standard deviation, standard error or custom. A scatter chart takes bars in x and in y.

In 2D charts that are not stacked, but the pie: linear, logarithmic, polynomial (with an order), power, exponential and moving average (with a period). Shows the equation and R², which can be dragged, and a label.

Slices selected by a click, Cmd-A, Cmd or Shift, and a color or texture per slice. Labels with a distance from the center in percent of the radius, the name of the series, and values in percent. Slices pulled out by dragging, a shadow per slice or for the group, and a rotation angle.
Space between bars and between sets, in percent of the thickness, also adjustable by dragging the bar. A shadow per bar or per group, and the names of the series.
Symbols (circle, triangle, square, diamond) with a size, and points joined by straight lines or curves.
A pair of columns per series, with separate colors for points, line and trendline.
Each of the two series can be a column, line or area. Axis Y1 on the left and Y2 on the right, formatted separately.
View angle, lighting style, depth and beveled edges on the pie.

A sender field shows data of the person who sends and is filled by itself from My Card when the document opens. A merge field shows data of the recipient. Without the data on the card, the field keeps showing its own label.
column6: Partial: sender outside the 15 kinds of ODF

column4: Dragging a card or vCard onto a sender field applies that card to every sender field. Data from Numbers cannot be a sender.
Dragging a card or vCard onto a merge field fills every field of the document. Another card dragged replaces the data. The original does not change and can be used again.

column3: Merging a group or several cards
column4: Edit > Mail Merge with a group or All, or dragging the group or several cards onto a field. The dialog offers New Document (a section per contact) or Send to Printer, and an option to replace a missing datum by another (for example, the work address in place of the home one).

Edit > Mail Merge > Numbers Document. For each field, the user picks in the Merge window the Target Name, which is a column header of the table. Then prints, and can repeat with another document. With facing pages, double-sided printing can put two recipients on the same sheet.
column6: Partial: a source in another document

column4: Clicking a field and typing replaces the field with the text. Save As keeps the changed version, and Undo Typing brings the field back.

Insert > Sender Field or Merge Field, or the Add (+) button in the Merge pane of the Link Inspector. The field starts highlighted, and the Target Name chooses the category of the datum or the Numbers column.

Changing a sender field into a merge field needs deleting it and making another. Delete removes the field. In the Mail Merge window, the table of fields changes the variant (work, home or other). The label of the field can be rewritten.
column6: Partial: a label apart from the value

column4: More than 50 fields: parts of the name, nickname, maiden name, job title, department, company, phones, emails, URLs, birthday, AIM and Yahoo accounts, addresses (work, home and other) and note. Several take synonyms, as Surname for Last name. The "first available" fields take the first value that exists on the card. The same table of names is in the Numbers guide.
Reference printer, paper size, custom sizes with a name and margins of their own or of the printer, orientation and scale in percent.
A thumbnail in the print dialog, with arrows to navigate, and "Open PDF in Preview" to see it at full size.
Printer, copies, collate, all pages or a range.
With the comments shown, or with the comments and changes pane open, the printed pages make room for the bubbles.

Keeps the fonts. Links become links in the PDF, as do the table of contents entries, footnotes and endnotes, web and email addresses, and bookmarks. Three image qualities: no reduction, 150 dpi or 72 dpi, with JPEG compression (0.7 and 0.9) for images without transparency. Takes a new password.

The number of pages can change, and tables, special typography and charts with transparency can come out differently. Charts become MS Graph objects that can be edited in Word. The format written (.doc or .docx) will be checked on the VM.
RTF keeps most of the formatting and the images. Plain text loses all formatting and the images.
The password of the document does not go to the exported file. Only PDF can take a new password.

Word processing documents only. Each chapter starts on a new page, and the ePub table of contents comes from the styles checked in the table of contents of the Document Inspector. Objects must be inline, and pending changes are accepted. Asks for title, author and genre and can use the first page as the cover (the content then starts on the second). The ePub does not reopen in Pages.
Save As > "Save a copy as", in Word format. The copy in iWork '08 format is out of scope.
Share with guests (comments, download, download formats and online password), publish at a public URL or keep for private use, and a list of Shared Documents.
column6: Out of scope: service shut down

column4: Attaches a Pages, Word or PDF version to a new message. A Pages document with a password goes protected, and PDF or Word with a password are not accepted. On Linux, the system email portal opens the user's client with the attachment.
Attaches a PDF or the Pages file to an iWeb blog or podcast.

Orientation, page and section layout, margins, page numbering, background graphics (watermarks), text, table of contents and list styles, object fills and lines, chart colors and styles, table appearance, and additional template pages.
Paper and orientation (envelopes included), facing page margins, headers and footers, master objects and alignment guides.

Every template defines paragraph, character and list styles, the table of contents, and the default text box, shape, table, chart and imported image. The Blank and Blank Canvas templates are starting points.
Format the text, the object and the text wrap and use Format > Advanced > Define Default Text Box Style (or Shape Style). Line length and direction are not part of the default.

Rows, columns, gridlines, text styles and shadow. Each attribute applies to a whole area (header row and column, inner and outer borders): changing a single cell does not enter the default. Format > Advanced > Define Default Table Style.
A default style for each chart type and the choice of the type that Insert > Chart creates ("Make the type the default").
Shadow, opacity, border, reflection, frame and text wrap of imported images (Define Default Image Style).

Text in blocks marked with Format > Advanced > Define as Placeholder Text. To edit an existing one, turn placeholder text authoring on and then off. If the selection includes the end of the paragraph, the whole paragraph goes when the user types, and the new text takes on the next paragraph.
A formatted and placed picture, movie or sound marked with Define as Media Placeholder. Media dragged onto it takes its size, position and frame, fitted by the mask (OBJ, pp. 140–141).

A layout of one or more pages between section breaks becomes a template section, with a name and a page count. It can leave the original document and stays available in the Pages button of word processing templates.
Rename, reorder and delete captured sections.

The new document opens exactly as saved, including the styles drawer, invisibles, rulers and layout marks. The default folder is My Templates, and each subfolder becomes a category in the Template Chooser. Deleting the file deletes the template. In Desk Writer, the folder is in the user's data directory (XDG).

Copying a table in one application and pasting it in another keeps its appearance, data and attributes. Hidden rows and columns do not appear at the destination (Numbers and Keynote say they are removed), and Numbers cell comments are not copied. In Keynote, pasting a table from Pages or Numbers creates a new table on the slide.
column6: A single table model (cells, formats, formulas and styles) and a clipboard format shared by the three.

column4: A chart copied from Numbers and pasted in Pages or Keynote stays linked to the source tables. The Numbers document must be saved before copying and after each change. Refresh reloads the data, Unlink turns the chart into a plain chart (edited in the Data Editor) and the Source link opens the Numbers document.
column6: A single chart engine and a lasting link to tables of another document, written as an extension in ODF.

column3: Numbers as the mail merge source
column4: A Numbers table feeds the Pages merge fields, with each field linked to a column header.
column6: Desk Writer reads Desk Tables tables without opening the application, so the table document model must exist as a library.

column4: Dragging Address Book cards or a group onto a table with headers that use Address Book field names adds a row per contact, even if repeated. Dragging onto the empty area creates a new table with Last Name, First Name, Phone and Email visible and the other columns hidden. The names and synonyms are the same as in the Pages mail merge.
column6: A shared contacts module (Evolution Data Server and vCard) with a single table of names and synonyms.

column4: The tables of the three applications use the same iWork functions (more than 250), described in their own guide, the iWork Formulas and Functions User Guide, opened from the Help menu of any of them.
column6: A single formula engine, with the same syntax and the same functions in the three.

column4: Media Browser, the system Fonts and Colors windows, the Inspector and the format bar appear in the three with the same function.
column6: Shared interface components, instead of three implementations.

column4: Shapes, text boxes, images with mask and Instant Alpha, shadow, reflection, frames, opacity, fills, sound, movie, and copy and paste style appear in the three guides. The behavior side by side will be checked on the VM.
column6: A single model of graphic objects and effects, with the same renderer on screen, in print and in PDF.

column4: The three insert equations through MathType 6, when installed, and then treat them as images.
column6: An equation editor of our own, shared, written as MathML.

column4: The three have placeholder text and media and default objects in templates. Keynote adds object placeholders on masters.
column6: A shared mechanism for placeholders and for the default style per object type.

column4: PDF, Mail, iWork.com and iWeb follow the same pattern in the three, each with its own formats (Word in Pages, Excel and CSV in Numbers, PowerPoint and others in Keynote).
column6: A shared PDF, print and send service, with filters of each application.

column4: Document password and archived versions (Lion) appear in the three. The copy in iWork '08 format is out of scope.
column6: A shared file service: password, automatic saving and version history.
column7: Automatic saving and versions, as in iWork 15 (D-001): the document saves itself, and the versions are browsed and restored from the main menu, the same in the three applications

column4: A table with a checkbox, slider, stepper or pop-up menu is copied to Pages or Keynote, which do not have these formats. No guide says what happens. The likely result is that the value stays (TRUE or FALSE, the number or the chosen item) with another format. To be checked on the VM.
column6: The control as a cell format in the shared model, and a copy rule for the applications that do not show it.

column4: Rows hidden by a filter stay hidden and, like the other hidden rows, should be left out of the copy. No guide says what happens to category rows, subtotals and collapsed categories. To be checked on the VM.
column6: Filters and categories in the shared model. On a copy to Desk Writer or Desk Slides, the paste decides what becomes a plain row, a fixed value or a formula.

column3: Formula that refers to another table
column4: The formulas guide only describes references to another table and another sheet in Numbers. A formula with Table 2::B5, copied with the table to Pages or Keynote, may become a value, an error or a broken reference. To be checked on the VM.
column6: References with sheet and table in the shared engine and, on copy, the same rule as iWork.

column4: A formula such as =SUM(2006) names the column by its header, which Pages and Keynote also accept. To be checked on the VM whether the name survives the copy and what happens when the header text changes at the destination.
column6: The header name kept with the A1 reference and resolved the same way in the three.

column4: A Numbers table with a named style keeps its appearance in Pages and Keynote, which have no named styles. On the way back, Paste and Match Style applies the default style of the document. In Keynote, a new table uses the default table of the master.
column6: A table style by areas, with an optional name. Outside Desk Tables, the paste applies the style as direct formatting.

column4: Text with paragraph, character or list styles, in a text box or a cell, is pasted in Numbers, which has no styles. The expected result is to keep the appearance as direct formatting. To be checked on the VM. Keynote has no named styles either, and its case is IOP-25.
column6: A single rich text model, with optional named styles. Where there are no styles, the paste applies the formatting already resolved.

column4: A Pages table with pending changes in its cells is copied to Numbers or Keynote, which do not track changes. To be checked on the VM whether the final text, the original or both go.
column6: Change marks per cell, resolved on paste when the destination does not take them.

column3: Copying cells instead of the table
column4: Within an application, cells copied to another table replace the cells at the destination, and loose cells outside a table create a new table in Numbers and Keynote. Between applications, the guides do not say. To be checked on the VM, including whether formulas go as formulas or as values.
column6: A suite clipboard format for cell ranges, with values, formats and formulas, plus tab-separated text and HTML for other programs.

column4: An inline table that runs across pages or columns becomes a floating object on the sheet or slide, and in Keynote a table taller than the slide has nowhere to continue. The other way, Numbers says to place the insertion point before pasting, which in Pages should create an inline table. To be checked on the VM.
column6: A table that does not depend on its anchor. The destination application chooses position and size and, in Desk Writer, whether it goes inline or floating.

column4: A Numbers chart that reads two or more tables, or that shows hidden data, is pasted linked in Pages or Keynote, and Refresh rereads the saved document. No guide says what happens when a source table is renamed, moves to another sheet or is deleted, or whether the link holds when the chart is copied from Pages to Keynote. To be checked on the VM.
column6: A link that keeps the source document and the references with sheet and table, plus cached data so that the chart opens without the source.

column3: Pages or Keynote chart in Numbers
column4: A chart with internal data is pasted in Numbers, where every chart reads table cells. To be checked on the VM whether Numbers creates a table with the data, as it does with a new chart without a selection, or whether the chart keeps its own data.
column6: Turn the internal data into a source table when pasting in Desk Tables, or accept charts with internal data there too, as the VM shows.

column3: Animation of tables and charts from Numbers
column4: In Keynote, a pasted table can build in by row, column or cell, and a chart by series or by data set. With a linked chart, Refresh can change the number of series of a build already set up. To be checked on the VM.
column6: A stable identity for rows, columns, cells, series and data sets, so that the build stays right after a refresh.

column4: In Pages, each merge field picks a column header of a Numbers table. The guide does not say which table counts when the document has several sheets and tables. To be checked on the VM.
column6: Desk Writer lists the tables of a Desk Tables file by sheet and name, which depends on how the tables are kept in ODS (next section).

column3: Text between Pages and the body of a slide
column4: Pages text with paragraph, character and list styles, pasted in a Keynote placeholder, keeps its appearance (Paste) or takes that of the placeholder (Paste and Match Style). The other way, the body of a slide reaches Pages with bullets and levels, but without a named style. To be checked on the VM whether the levels become a Pages list and what paragraph style the text gets.
column6: The same rich text with optional styles (IOP-17). The paste resolves the styles into direct formatting when the destination does not have them, and the levels of the body map to the list levels of Desk Writer.

column4: Pages has an Outline mode, and in Keynote the title and bullets of each slide form an editable outline. No guide says what happens when a Pages outline is pasted in the Keynote Outline, which could create a slide per first level topic, or the other way. To be checked on the VM.
column6: Topic levels in rich text and a conversion between outline and slides in which the first level becomes the title and the following ones become body bullets, the same both ways.

column3: Slide objects in Pages or Numbers
column4: A shape, image, text box, movie or group copied from a slide keeps its appearance in Pages and Numbers, which have no builds, Magic Move or links to slides. To be checked on the VM what happens to builds, to a link to a slide and to a master placeholder, and whether the object arrives floating or inline in Pages.
column6: A single object model. The paste drops what the destination does not have, such as animations, and Desk Writer decides between inline and floating by the insertion point, as with tables (IOP-20).

column3: Pages or Numbers objects on a slide
column4: An inline object in Pages becomes floating on the slide, and the text wrap no longer applies. An image larger than the slide is scaled down when it enters Keynote (KOBJ-02), but the guide does not say whether this holds for objects pasted from another application. To be checked on the VM where the object lands and whether it is scaled down.
column6: Geometry in absolute units, a rule for objects larger than the slide, and the text wrap kept in the object even where it does not apply, for the way back to Desk Writer.

column4: Slides copied in the Navigator are pasted in another presentation together with their master (KMES-04). No guide says what happens when a copied slide is pasted in Pages or Numbers: an image of the slide, the loose objects or nothing. To be checked on the VM, including what becomes of the presenter notes and comments.
column6: A suite clipboard format for slides, with the master, notes and comments, and an image of the slide for the other applications and programs.

column4: A table, chart, shape or text box pasted from Pages or Numbers may keep its own appearance or take the default of the slide's master. The guide only says that new objects are created with the default (KMES-14 to KMES-17). To be checked on the VM, including with an object moved between slides of different masters or themes.
column6: Defaults scoped to the master, applied only when the object is created, unless the VM shows another rule.

column4: A movie or sound copied between the three applications should keep its start, end, poster, repeat and volume. In Keynote, it plays when the slide appears, unless a Start Movie or Start Audio build says otherwise, and in Pages audio plays on a double click on the icon. The soundtrack and the recorded narration belong to the presentation and do not travel with objects. To be checked on the VM what happens to the build of a movie copied to Pages.
column6: A media object with the settings of the QuickTime Inspector (OBJ-19, KOBJ-11), and soundtrack and narration as presentation data, in Desk Slides only.

column4: Text or an object with a link to a slide, to end the presentation or to another presentation is copied to Pages or Numbers, which do not have these destinations. The other way, a Pages link to a bookmark reaches Keynote, which has no bookmarks. To be checked on the VM whether the link goes away, becomes inactive or stays in the file with no effect.
column6: Typed link destinations in the shared model. The proposal is to keep, inactive, the destination that the application does not use, so that it works again in the source application, unless the VM shows another rule.

column4: Magic Move links the same objects on successive slides, and the guide recommends duplicating the slide (KTRN-03). To be checked on the VM whether an object copied and pasted on the next slide, the same image inserted again and an object from Pages also take part in the effect.
column6: A shared object identity across slides, separate from xml:id, created when duplicating or copying within the suite and written in desk:.

column4: The window works on the Desk minimum screen, 1280 × 720, and adapts to smaller windows, such as half a screen: the sidebar and then the Inspector become overlay panes, and the object buttons of the header bar go into the Insert menu. Phones and screens smaller than the minimum are not supported; the application opens on them with a notice (GNM-14).
column7: M+: below 720 px the navigation sidebar becomes an overlay and the object buttons go into the Insert menu; below 520 px the Inspector becomes an overlay too

column4: Notices that need no answer, such as document saved or page deleted, appear in a toast, with Undo when the action can be undone.

column3: Unsaved documents at the end of the session
column4: With a changed and unsaved document, the app holds back the end of the session and shutdown (gtk_application_inhibit) until the person decides.

column3: Objects, tables and charts for the screen reader
column4: Shapes, images, text boxes, media, tables and charts appear in the accessibility tree, with role, name and description. Images and objects have alternative text that can be edited in the Inspector.
A thumbnailer shows the first page of .pages and ODT documents in Files, the equivalent of Quick Look, without needing LibreOffice.
A LocalSearch extractor indexes the text and the information (author, title, keywords) of .pages documents, as Spotlight did (DOC-19).
The GNOME Shell search lists the recent documents of each app and opens the chosen one in it.
Paragraphs in Hebrew, Persian and Arabic run from right to left, with alignment, indents and tabs mirrored, and the interface mirrors in these languages, including the ruler and the Inspector.
The interface is translated into the languages of po/LANGUAGES.md, once each app has all its features.

The Sidebar button only shows and hides the sidebar and Insert sits beside it in the header bar; Format and Arrange are in the Format pane and the context menu, the writing tools in the context menu, and the main menu holds only what belongs to the file and the application, with View as a submenu. A command search finds any of their items by name.
column5: Architecture: conflicts between parity and the HIG
column7: M+: the Sidebar button is a toggle and Insert sits beside it; View is a submenu of the main menu; Format and Arrange are tabs of the Format pane and the context menu; the main menu holds the file and the application. The command search opens from the main menu and with Ctrl+/ (confirmed on 14 November)

column4: The shortcuts window uses the current Libadwaita dialog in place of GtkShortcutsWindow, and the minimum versions in the README match the GNOME 51 runtime target.

A pane the height of the window, on the left, with its own header. The content switcher chooses between Pages (thumbnails), Styles, Comments and Search results, and the + button inserts a template page. F9 shows and hides the sidebar, which goes away in full screen and becomes an overlay below 720 px.

There is no bottom bar: a zoom control sits over a corner of the document, and the word count over its foot, showing that of the selection when there is one. Both stay out of the way of the text and keep the look of the osd style of GNOME.

column3: Notice of a screen smaller than the minimum
column4: When a window opens on a monitor with fewer than 1280 × 720 logical pixels (after the display scale), a bar under the top bars says that the screen is below the Desk minimum resolution and that parts of the window may not fit. The application keeps working, and the Close button hides the bar until the next launch.
column7: M+ (docs/interface/proposals)

column4: Edit > Deselect All (Shift-Cmd-A) clears the text and object selection, the inverse of Select All.
column7: Ctrl+Shift+A, the shortcut the HIG gives this command

column4: Format > Reapply Defaults to Selection gives the selected object back the default style that the template defines for its type (MOD-04 to MOD-07).
Format > Text Box > Hide Connection Lines hides and shows the lines that join linked text boxes (OBJ-15).

column3: Reset text and object handles of a shape
column4: Format > Shape > Reset Text and Object Handles makes the text horizontal and the selection box aligned after rotating a shape, as in Keynote (KTXT-06).

View > Enter Screen View (Shift-Cmd-R) hides the page edges, margins, headers and footers, and the text flows to the width of the window; objects that move with the text show whatever their wrap: inline ones stay in the line, the others go after the paragraph they are anchored to, centred at their size (a text box or a rectangle with text takes the width of the column and the height of its text), back in place on leaving; objects fixed on a page are hidden, on any page, and objects in the text can be selected and dragged to another place in it. A short notice says "Screen View is on", or that some content is hidden when something is, and leaving says "Screen View is off". Zoom becomes Auto, by the width of the window, with View > Text Size (Auto, Bigger, Smaller) stepping from 80% to 310%; thumbnails, ruler, page templates, Show Layout, Go To and Add Page are off, and no page count shows. It also works in full screen, where the column grows with the window, and Preferences can open new documents in it.
column5: Pages 15.4 (18 and 21 November, steps 19 and 19e of W1)
column7: The notices are toasts (GNM-02); the shortcut is Ctrl+Shift+R

column3: Live table of contents in the sidebar
column4: View > Table of Contents opens a page of the sidebar listing the paragraphs in heading styles, with Edit and Insert Table of Contents; with no heading it says how to fill it. A paragraph given a heading style appears at once, and typing in a heading updates its entry as it is typed. Long entries end in an ellipsis.

Preferences > General > Default Font, "Set font and size for new Basic documents", asks for a font (Helvetica Neue by default) and a size (11 pt by default). The size sets the Body style of new documents from the Basic templates, and the other paragraph styles scale with it.
column7: In the Preferences dialog, with the font chooser of GNOME

column3: Gradient and image fill of text
column4: The Text Color row offers Text Color, Gradient Fill, Advanced Gradient Fill, Image Fill and Advanced Image Fill, as the fill of an object does. A gradient has two colors, a swap button and an angle (270 degrees by default), and "Apply gradient to entire page" lays it over the page so that the lines continue it. An image fill tiles by default at 50 %, with the usual scale modes; the advanced one adds a tint.

Capitalization in the text options offers None, All Caps, Small Caps, Title Case and Start Case. Title Case leaves short joining words in lower case; Start Case capitalizes every word. They change how the text is drawn, not its characters. Edit > Transformations changes the characters: Make Upper Case, Make Lower Case, Capitalize.

Drop Cap in the Style tab of the text, per paragraph: 3 lines and 1 character by default, the font and color of the text, the text wrapped around the shape of the letter. Options: raised lines, wrap by the shape or the rectangle, extra spacing, outdent into the margin, and a background shape with border, character scale (80 %) and corner radius (20 %). Six built-in styles of drop cap, and the current one can be saved as a new style.
column6: Native (style:drop-cap), shape and styles by extension

column4: With "Automatically format fractions" on (off by default), a fraction typed and followed by a space or punctuation becomes the precomposed character of Unicode when there is one: 1/2 gives ½, 5/8 gives ⅝, 0/3 gives ↉. A fraction without such a character (13/16, 2/4), inside a word or after another digit stays as typed.
Smart quotes are on by default, and two lists choose the double and the single quotes. Quotes already typed are converted with Replace All or Replace in Selection of the substitutions panel.
column7: The settings are in the Preferences dialog; converting is a command of the Edit menu and of Search Commands, since GNOME has no substitutions panel

column3: Language and region of the document
column4: File > Advanced > Language & Region opens a sheet with the language (System by default) and the region, and a preview of a date, a time, a number and an amount. The language sets the words of dates and where the currency symbol goes; the region sets the separators and the short date. It is saved with the document.
column6: Native (fo:language and fo:country of the default style)
column7: A dialog of the main menu

column3: Default text box appearance of the document
column4: Format > Advanced > Set as Default Text Box Appearance makes the selected box the look of the new text boxes of the document.
column6: Native (default style of the graphic family)

column3: Dragging list items by the bullet
column4: A click on a bullet selects the text of its item. Dragging the bullet moves the item with its sub-items: a blue line with a triangle marks where it goes, and where the triangle sits sets the level it takes. The item stays selected after the drop.

Columns in the Layout tab of the text: with no selection they apply to the whole section, page long and not balanced. With paragraphs selected in the middle, two layout breaks enclose them and their columns are balanced; when the selection runs to the end, one break comes before it and the columns fill down the page.

A selected box has a circle on its top edge. Clicking it starts a thread, shown as a badge with the order of the box in the color of the thread; clicking the circle of another box adds it to the thread, and its text continues the thread. The badge opens a menu with the threads (named after their first words), Layout Order, Create New Thread and Remove from Thread. Several threads can live in a document, each in its color, numbered from 1.

The Table button shows the table styles as thumbnails, on pages; a click inserts a table of that style, inline with the text, with a header row and column. The Table tab of the Format pane shows the styles, six to a page, and Format > Advanced > Create Table Style saves one.
Title in the table options puts "Table 1" (the name of the table) centered above it, inside the table object; Outline Table Title draws a line around it.
Arrange > Lock and Unlock, also in the Arrange tab, for a table that is not inline. A locked table cannot be moved, resized or edited, and the Format pane only shows Unlock.
column7: Ctrl+L and Ctrl+Shift+Alt+L, the shortcuts of Desk for the other objects (OBJ-32)

column4: Cells dragged out of a table onto the page make a new floating table with only those cells, the style of the source and its title setting, under the next default name. The cells are moved: the source keeps them only when Option is held.

Create Custom Format in the Data Format list opens a sheet with name, type (number, date and time, text), rules and tokens to drag (integer, decimal, scale, currency, space); the scale is percent, hundreds, thousands, millions, billions or trillions, with or without their symbol, or scientific. The format is then listed by name, with Edit Custom Format.
